name: SOA
label: Dischord
lede: Ten songs on a seven-inch, paid for out of a Georgetown ice cream manager's wages, by a band that was finished before its first birthday.

eras.title: The roadie takes the mic
eras.text: Henry Garfield spent 1980 hauling gear for The Teen Idles and scooping ice cream in Georgetown. When Minor Threat poached Lyle Preslar from the Extorts, the three players left behind went looking for a singer, and found Garfield, the scene's most intense fan.

years.h: Henry Garfield, Teen Idles roadie, gets a turn at the mic
years.p: Henry Garfield is carrying amps for [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]] when singer Nathan Strejcek misses a practice, and Garfield talks the band into letting him sing. It's a rehearsal, not a gig, but it plants the idea.

q: We're too scared to approach him.
years.h: The Extorts find Henry Garfield behind an ice cream counter
years.p: [[Lyle Preslar|c1b9b78e-691f-424d-8ce1-53c87c24d299]] leaves the Extorts to play guitar with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] in what becomes [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]. [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]], Wendel Blow and Simon Jacobsen recruit Henry Garfield, and SOA is born.
years.xp:
The three Extorts knew exactly who they wanted and were too intimidated to ask him. They sent [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] as go-between, and the meeting happened at the Häagen-Dazs in Georgetown where Garfield was working as a manager. Michael Hampton remembered him as the Teen Idles' roadie guy.

After that it was practice every other day: parents' basements, Dischord House, even rooms in Kalorama mansions. Garfield, Hampton said later, always charmed the moms.

years.h: SOA's first show gives the D.C. scene a harder edge
years.p: SOA play out for the first time in December 1980. Dischord's own history says the band brought a new level of aggression to the music, matching the mood of the scene's younger kids exactly.

years.h: SOA play the Unheard Music Festival at d.c. space
years.p: SOA play two nights of the Unheard Music Festival at d.c. space, the downtown arts space, in the band's first month on stage.

eras.title: Ice cream money and a one-way ticket
eras.text: SOA lasted about as long as a school year. In that time they made Dischord's second record, paid for by singer Henry Garfield, and played their final show on the same night Garfield stepped into Black Flag, the band that would take him to California.

years.p: SOA play the 9:30 Club on F Street, one of the handful of shows the band ever played.

years.src: Dischord Records · Wikipedia · WJLA oral history
years.p: SOA's only record: ten songs on a seven-inch, recorded at Inner Ear with Skip Groff. Henry Garfield paid for the recording and the pressing himself.
years.xp:
Tina Angelos shot the cover photo; Michael Hampton and Chris Edwards designed the sleeve.

Dischord was only one record old, with [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]]' Minor Disturbance as No. 1. The label had no money for a second release, and Garfield had a steady paycheck from Häagen-Dazs. [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] later put it simply: the ice cream job funded Dischord's second record.

The session work ran from December 1980 into January 1981. The EP went out of print on vinyl long ago, but the songs have never been hard to find: Dischord has kept them in circulation on compilations ever since.

years.h: Ivor Hanson takes the drums; SOA rehearse at the Naval Observatory
years.p: [[Ivor Hanson|a17981f7-ab3d-46dc-859a-582ac894cb20]] takes over SOA's drums from Simon Jacobsen. Hanson's father is a U.S. Navy admiral, so the band rehearses at the Naval Observatory. By Hanson's own count, he plays exactly one show with SOA.

q: Henry's last show with SOA was his first show with Black Flag.
years.src: Dischord Records · WJLA oral history · Wikipedia
years.h: SOA's last show: Philadelphia, opening for [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]]
years.p: SOA open for Black Flag in Philadelphia, Henry Garfield sings with Black Flag too, and the night ends in a riot. SOA break up that month.
years.xp:
Dischord's history records the riot plainly. The oral history puts it down to tensions with the neighborhood around the venue, not to anything that happened on stage. It was one of only a handful of SOA shows: the WJLA oral history counts about five, Wikipedia about a dozen.

For drummer Ivor Hanson, the show was a hinge: Garfield sang SOA songs to open and then sang with Black Flag. It was the end of SOA and the start of Garfield's next band.

years.p: Henry Garfield passes a [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] audition at Tu Casa Studio, quits Häagen-Dazs, takes the surname Rollins, and plays his first official Black Flag show at the Cuckoo's Nest in Costa Mesa, California.
years.xp:
Garfield had been a Black Flag fan since getting the Nervous Breakdown EP. Before the audition, Dez Cadena let him up to sing Clocked In with the band at a New York bar show.

Rollins was a name he and [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] had used as teenagers.

years.h: Michael Hampton and Ivor Hanson go straight into [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]]
years.p: With Henry Garfield gone west, [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]] and [[Ivor Hanson|a17981f7-ab3d-46dc-859a-582ac894cb20]] start Faith with [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]] and [[Chris Bald|0838359b-95a7-48e9-a9f6-0e8f40bb34d2]]. The Hampton and Hanson partnership runs on through Faith and [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]].

eras.title: The records outlive the band
eras.text: SOA were gone before most of D.C. had heard them on vinyl. Dischord kept the songs moving anyway, first on the sampler that defined the early scene and then on a 12-inch that gathered the label's first singles.

years.h: Three SOA songs on Flex Your Head
years.p: I Hate the Kids, Disease and Stepping Stone Party land on Dischord's compilation of the early D.C. bands, next to [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]], [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]] and [[Void|960a1d2f-2b5f-4fcf-bf11-4957529a6508]].
Dischord reissues SOA's No Policy on Four Old 7"s on a 12", gathering the label's earliest singles onto one LP.

eras.title: The vault opens
eras.text: Once Dischord started mining its own history, SOA came back into print again and again. The last surprise was the band's very first recording session, released more than three decades after it happened.

years.h: SOA's No Policy on CD for the first time
years.p: No Policy joins Dischord's other 1981 singles on Dischord 1981: The Year in Seven Inches.

years.h: SOA's Public Defender makes the box set
years.p: Dischord picks SOA's Public Defender for 20 Years of Dischord, its anniversary box of the label's bands.

years.h: SOA's first session, taped in 1980, comes out in 2014
years.p: SOA recorded eight songs with Skip Groff at Inner Ear on December 29, 1980. Two takes went on Flex Your Head and one on No Policy; the full session finally comes out on colored vinyl.
years.xp: Five of the eight songs had never been heard in these versions. More than 33 years on, the first SOA recording became the last SOA release.
